events.title: Napoleon Abdicates and Signs the Treaty of Fontainebleau
events.description: Following the capture of Paris by Coalition forces, Napoleon Bonaparte signed the Treaty of Fontainebleau, confirming his abdication as Emperor of the French. The treaty exiled him to the Mediterranean island of Elba, where he was granted sovereignty over the island.
events.significance: Marked the end of Napoleon's first reign and the apparent close of the Napoleonic Wars, though he would escape Elba in 1815 and return for the Hundred Days before his final defeat at Waterloo.

events.title: Titanic Departs Queenstown on Her Maiden Voyage
events.description: RMS Titanic made her final port call at Queenstown (now Cobh), Ireland, where she picked up additional passengers and mail before heading into the Atlantic Ocean. It was the last stop before the ship struck an iceberg on the night of April 14.
events.significance: The sinking of the Titanic, which killed more than 1,500 people, led to major reforms in maritime safety, including the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).

events.title: Liberation of Buchenwald Concentration Camp
events.description: Prisoners at Buchenwald took control of the camp as American forces of the US Third Army approached, and soldiers of the 6th Armored Division entered the camp shortly afterward. Tens of thousands of surviving inmates were freed.
events.significance: The liberation revealed the scale of Nazi atrocities to the Allied world and became a key part of the documentation of the Holocaust, shaping post-war justice and memory.

events.title: Civil Rights Act of 1968 Signed into Law
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1968, known as the Fair Housing Act, which prohibited discrimination in the sale, rental, and financing of housing based on race, religion, and national origin. It was signed days after the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
events.significance: Extended federal civil rights protections to housing and remains a cornerstone of US anti-discrimination law, later expanded to cover sex, disability, and familial status.

events.title: Apollo 13 Launches
events.description: NASA launched Apollo 13 from Kennedy Space Center with astronauts Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise, intended as the third crewed lunar landing. An oxygen tank exploded two days later, forcing the mission to abort the landing.
events.significance: The safe return of the crew became a landmark in crisis management and engineering ingenuity, often called a 'successful failure,' and it led to safety improvements in the space program.
